A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for estimating authoritativeness of documents based on textual features, and have shown how this method can be used in conjunction with link analysis to provide a more robust and complete estimate of document authoritativeness.

we have developed a new method for estimating a document's authority based on its textual content, and we have shown how to combine these estimates with link analysis to provide a more robust estimate of a document's authority.
we have developed a method for estimating authoritativeness that is complementary to link analysis and that is useful for "high-value content search."
The main takeaway from our work is that
the textual content of a document contains information about the authoritativeness that can be used to estimate the authoritativeness and rank documents.
there are a large number of textual cues to a document's authorativeness that can be computed and used in a variety of ways to improve search results.
the use of textual features for the estimation of authoritativeness is a promising approach for improving the performance of Web search engines.
